learning_outcomes.text: Understand the operation of electronic components in linear regime.
Know, understand, and analyze the operation of the different fundamental blocks that form the basis of electronic design and the aspects that affect their performance.
Learn the concepts of amplification, frequency response, and feedback in analog amplifiers.
Show the influence of different capacitances (physical and parasitic) on the frequency response of different electronic blocks.
Identify the different feedback topologies, analyzing their influence on circuit performance and recognizing their advantages and disadvantages.
Know how to use operational amplifiers and some of their applications.

syllabus_topics: Design, specifications, and applications of analog circuits.
Review of operation mode and modeling of bipolar and MOS transistors.
Use of transistors in simple gain stages.
Methodology for analyzing the influence of different capacitances (physical and parasitic) on the frequency response of analog circuits.
Study of electronic blocks for designing more complex analog circuits, based on simple amplifier structures.
General structure of a feedback circuit.
Advantages and disadvantages of feedback.
Guidelines for analyzing feedback circuits.
Analysis of different structures with operational amplifiers.

Course Evaluation System
Necessary Material for Development
Review of Necessary Prior Knowledge
Concept of amplification, transfer curve, biasing, voltage, current, power amplifiers, and efficiency
Concepts of small-signal and large-signal operation. Concept of distortion
Biasing networks
Basic structures, high and low impedance terminals
Common emitter (source), common base (gate), common collector (drain) amplifier structures
Frequency spectrum of signals
Amplifier transfer function
Frequency response of single time constant networks
Concept of dominant and secondary pole
Approximate determination of time constants: open-circuit and short-circuit time constants
Frequency response of amplifiers
Concept of power amplifier: requirements
Operation in class A, B, and class AB
Transfer curves, power dissipation, and efficiency in power conversion
BJT and MOS-based structure, operation, large-signal analysis
Differential signal response, differential gain, offset, mismatches
Common-mode signal response, concept of CMRR, common-mode input range (CMR)
Differential pairs with active loads
General structure and analysis of a feedback system, advantages and disadvantages of feedback
Analysis of different feedback topologies
Effect of feedback on system poles, instability, and compensation

assessment_methods.method: Delivery and defense of a project

assessment_rules: For continuous evaluation, the final exam accounts for 55% and requires a minimum score of 4 out of 10; if this minimum is not met but the total score is above 5, the final grade will be 4.5. Practical reports contribute 15% and are not recoverable, requiring attendance to sessions. The project contributes 30% and is recoverable, allowing students to improve their grade in the extraordinary call.
